newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INTERVIEW-Singapore Power to make strong phone bid.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Singapore Power to make strong phone bid.

text.p: The chairman of state electricity and gas utility Singapore Power, Ho Kwon Ping, said on Wednesday the company was confident it could put in a strong bid for a licence to run a telephone service in Singapore.
"We are confident that we would be able to put together a very strong team," Ho told Reuters in an interview.
"We think that the four parties in this consortium are very strong and therefore we are confident that we are able to put in a strong bid," he added.

Singapore Power, state-owned Singapore Technologies Telemedia (STT), British Telecommunications Plc and Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp said last month they had formed a consortium to bid for the city-state's second basic telecommunication service licence.
The Singapore government has said it will allow one or two new groups to operate fixed line telephone services from 2000 to compete with the current monopoly Singapore Telecommunications Ltd.
The government is expected to short-list candidates bidding for the licences in September and award them sometime in 1998.
"Singapore power is very strong in terms of the entire infrastructure that we provide," Ho said.

"Singapore Technologies Telemedia (STT) is strong. It is a Singapore company with regional experience in telecommunications. British Telecom is a global player. NTT is also (one of) the largest players in Japan," Ho said.
Three other groups have also signalled interest in bidding for a Singapore licence.
These groups include diversified Singapore maritime conglomerate SembCorp, Britain's Cable & Wireless, Hong Kong Telecommunications, Keppel Telecom and Singapore Press Holdings.
Asked how much money his consortium planned to invest initially in the joint venture, Ho said the consortium had yet to come up with any figures.
But he quoted analysts as saying the consortium was expected to invest between Singapore $1 billion and $1.5 billion to replicate Singapore Telecom's infrastructure.
Asked about profitability of the joint venture, Ho said in light of keener competition it would not be as profitable now as it would have been a year ago.
